title: Draft-tick triage: a signal becomes a proposal a human accepts or discards
description:
The human gate between 'something arrived' and 'the factory spent money on it'.

An ingested signal lands as a DRAFT tick and is presented in the operator channel with inline Create and Dispatch buttons. Create accepts it into the tracker as a normal open tick; Dispatch accepts it and starts a run. Discard leaves nothing behind but the dedup record, so the same signal does not re-propose forever.

Why a draft rather than a tick with a flag: a draft has not entered the ready queue, so it cannot be picked up by tk next or swept into a wave before a human has looked. Make that property structural rather than conventional.

Inline callbacks carry the question/draft id, so routing is unambiguous even in a shared chat (this is why it does not depend on the free-text rules). It DOES depend on spq's project legibility — a Create button under a message that does not say which project it belongs to is a trap.
